- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >2% from 14-day moving average of history, adjust forecast toward historical mean (not latest peak or trough).
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day price and sentiment to anchor forecast.
